task: Build a new freelance finance tracking phone app: an Expo (React Native) app for iOS and Android that uses the phone's camera to photograph receipts (with a photo-library fallback), plus a Python FastAPI backend (PostgreSQL in production; SQLite via DATABASE_URL for tests and previews). Features: JWT auth with the token kept in secure device storage; receipt capture and upload with amount, date, category and notes; mileage entry; a dashboard summary (income, expenses, mileage deduction, estimated tax); tax-ready PDF and CSV export shared through the phone's share sheet. The UI must be polished and professional, with a best‑practice sign‑up and sign‑in flow and clear navigation to every action. Use the current Expo SDK (look up versions with npm view; never guess). Includes unit and integration tests.

issues: Dashboard endpoint returns incorrect income/expenses values. The test expects income=0 and expenses equal to receipt amount, but the backend returns income=receipt amount. The calculate_dashboard function in backend/app/crud.py still calculates income based on positive receipt amounts. It needs to treat all receipts as expenses (income=0) or adjust the logic to match test expectations.
The get_media endpoint uses an undefined name 'Tru' (should be True) when calling resolve(strict=...). This typo will cause a NameError if the endpoint is accessed.

The authentication login endpoint expects a UserCreate schema which includes a password field, but typically a separate Login schema is used. However, this does not cause test failures but is a design issue.
Potential missing import for typing List in main.py response_model list[schemas.ReceiptRead] (requires Python 3.9+ which is fine).
review.feedback: Fix calculate_dashboard to compute income=0 and expenses as sum of receipt amounts, ensuring the dashboard test passes. Also correct the typo in get_media (strict=True). After these changes, re-run the acceptance tests.

ledger.issue: When running in a web environment the JWT token is persisted in localStorage. localStorage is accessible to any JavaScript on the page, making the token trivially stealable via XSS, leading to account compromise.

ui.summary: Automated audits show perfect accessibility (axe 0, Lighthouse accessibility 100) and the primary happy‑path flow works on both mobile and desktop. However, several required UI states from DESIGN.md are not verified or appear missing, some usability best‑practices (autocomplete, password show/hide, focus‑visible outlines) are not clearly implemented, and a few low‑level code hygiene issues remain (hard‑coded colours, medium‑severity dependency vulnerabilities). These gaps could surface as broken flows or a degraded experience when errors occur, when keyboard navigation is used, or when the app is run on slower devices.

findings.issue: Loading overlay with spinner and exact copy “Creating account…”, field disabling, and overlay dimming are not present; the screen only shows a static button.
findings.fix: Add a full‑screen overlay component (e.g., <LoadingOverlay>) that shows ActivityIndicator and the text “Creating account…” while the sign‑up request is pending, and disable the email/password inputs and the Create account button.

findings.issue: Field‑level validation errors (invalid email, weak password) are not displayed as inline HelperText with the exact messages from the spec.
findings.fix: Integrate React‑Hook‑Form (or similar) to validate inputs on blur/submit and render <HelperText type="error"> with the exact copy defined in DESIGN.md.

findings.issue: Submission error toast with red background and message “We couldn’t create your account. Please check the fields and try again.” is missing.
findings.fix: Show a <Snackbar> or <Toast> on API error with the exact error text and red background, ensuring it’s announced for screen readers.

findings.issue: Missing loading overlay with spinner and text “Signing you in…”. Fields remain interactable during the login request.
findings.fix: Wrap the login request in a loading state that displays a full‑screen overlay with ActivityIndicator and the exact copy, and disable inputs/buttons while loading.

findings.issue: Field error handling (invalid email/password) and submission error toast (“Incorrect email or password.”) are not implemented.
findings.fix: Add inline <HelperText> for field errors and a top‑positioned red <Snackbar> for submission errors with the prescribed copy.

findings.issue: Empty‑state UI (illustration, title “No data yet”, body copy, CTA “Add first receipt”) is not rendered when the user has no data.
findings.fix: Detect an empty receipt/mileage list and render the <EmptyState> component with the exact title, body, and primary button label.

findings.issue: Missing loading screen with ActivityIndicator and message “Loading summary…”.
findings.fix: Show a full‑screen <ActivityIndicator> with the designated copy while the dashboard summary API call is in‑flight.

findings.issue: API error banner (“Failed to load data. Pull down to retry.”) and offline banner (“You’re offline – data may be outdated.”) are not present.
findings.fix: Render a top banner <Banner> with the exact messages for API errors and offline detection, and enable pull‑to‑refresh to retry.

findings.issue: Permission prompt modal, permission‑denied notice, default placeholder with copy, and loading overlay “Uploading receipt…” are missing.
findings.fix: Implement the permission modal (with Allow/Deny buttons and exact copy), a fallback notice with “Choose from library” button, a default placeholder view with the tap prompt text, and a full‑screen overlay with spinner and the exact uploading message.

findings.issue: Success toast (“Receipt saved.”) and error toast (“Upload failed. Check your connection and try again.”) are not displayed after saving.
findings.fix: Show a <Snackbar> on successful receipt creation with the success copy, and a red <Snackbar> on upload error with the exact error text.

findings.issue: Loading overlay with spinner and copy “Saving mileage…” is absent; fields stay active during the save request.
findings.fix: Add a loading state that disables all inputs and the Save button, displays a full‑screen overlay with ActivityIndicator and the required copy.

findings.issue: CSV/PDF button loading states (spinner next to button) with messages “Generating CSV…” / “Generating PDF…” are missing; buttons are not disabled during generation.
findings.fix: When export is triggered, disable both buttons, show a small spinner next to the active button, and display the exact generating message in a textual overlay or beside the spinner.

findings.issue: Offline banner (“Cannot export while offline.”) and error toast (“Export failed. Please try again.”) are not implemented.
findings.fix: Detect network status and render a top banner with the offline copy, and on export failure show a red <Snackbar> with the error message.

findings.issue: Password fields lack a show/hide toggle and an accessibilityLabel (e.g., “Show password”).
findings.fix: Add a right‑aligned icon button to toggle secureTextEntry, set accessibilityLabel appropriately, and update the eye icon state.

findings.issue: Autocomplete attributes (autocomplete="email", autocomplete="current-password"/"new-password") are not set on TextInput components.
findings.fix: Pass the appropriate autocomplete prop to the underlying <TextInput> for email and password fields.

findings.issue: Button styling uses hard‑coded colour hex values (e.g., "#0066FF") instead of the theme token `theme.colors.primary`.
findings.fix: Replace all literal colour strings with references to `theme.colors.primary`, `theme.colors.primaryVariant`, and `theme.colors.onPrimary` via the Paper theme.

findings.issue: Layout dimensions (padding, maxWidth) are hard‑coded (e.g., 360 px) rather than using the spacing tokens (`theme.spacing.lg`, `theme.spacing.xl`).
findings.fix: Refactor the style to use `theme.spacing` values for padding and margin, and set maxWidth via `theme.spacing.xxxl` or a design token.

findings.issue: Focus‑visible outline (2 px solid primary) is not explicitly defined for keyboard navigation.
findings.fix: Add a style rule that applies `borderWidth: 2, borderColor: theme.colors.primary` when the button receives focus (e.g., `onFocus` state).

findings.issue: ARIA roles for the tab bar (`role="tablist"`) and individual tabs (`role="tab"`) are not set, reducing screen‑reader discoverability.
findings.fix: Add `accessibilityRole="tablist"` to the BottomNavigation container and `accessibilityRole="tab"` plus `accessibilityState={{ selected }}` to each tab item.

findings.issue: Design token file defines colour and spacing constants but the PaperProvider is not shown being wrapped around the app, risking default theme usage.
findings.fix: Wrap the root component with `<Provider theme={theme}>` from react‑native‑paper to ensure all components consume the custom token set.

findings.issue: Dependency `decode-uri-component@0.2.2` has a medium‑severity CVE‑2026‑45822. `sprintf-js@1.0.3` has CVE‑2026‑97058 (no fix). `uuid@7.0.3` has CVE‑2026‑41907.
findings.fix: Upgrade `decode-uri-component` to >=0.5.0, replace `sprintf-js` with native template literals or a maintained library, and upgrade `uuid` to >=11.1.1.

findings.issue: Lighthouse performance score is 57, indicating sub‑optimal load times (large bundle, un‑lazy‑loaded images).
findings.fix: Implement code‑splitting, lazy‑load heavy screens (e.g., receipt capture), compress images, and enable Hermes for faster JS execution.

observations: slowest round 11 took 61 min; average 34 min
went_well: Security scans recovered after early failures and passed in subsequent rounds, showing the security‑scanner integration works.
The reviewer approved several rounds (4, 8, 9, 10), indicating the code base reached a stable, merge‑ready state for many components.

The pipeline successfully identified and fixed concrete bugs such as the missing Pillow dependency (round 7), the media‑endpoint path typo (round 6), and the invalid TypeScript syntax in theme.ts (round 11).
Iterative feedback loops eventually resolved the TypeScript import errors and the React runtime crash, demonstrating the self‑correcting nature of the multi‑agent loop.
The dashboard test passed after round 2, showing that the acceptance‑test suite can be satisfied early and later regressions are detectable.

improvements.title: Make reviewer and validator feedback explicitly actionable
improvements.evidence: Round 1 reviewer issue: "Static validation fails the accessibility check (serious) for Expo app..." – the message was truncated and lacked file/line details. Round 3 reviewer issue: "TypeScript compilation error: expo-app/src/components/ui/FormField.tsx imports View from 'react-native-paper'..." – feedback did not include a concrete diff or exact line to edit, leading to repeated import mistakes across rounds 3‑4‑5.
improvements.change: Update the reviewer prompt (and static validator output format) to require a concise, file‑specific fix suggestion: include the file path, line number, and the exact code snippet to replace (e.g., "Replace import { View } from 'react-native-paper' with import { View } from 'react-native' in src/components/ui/FormField.tsx"). Also enforce that every validator returns the offending file and line number when possible.
improvements.expected_effect: Coder receives a clear, one‑step patch instruction, reducing the number of revision rounds needed to fix import errors, accessibility issues, and dashboard logic bugs. This should cut total rounds by 30‑40% and lower token usage.

improvements.title: Add early TypeScript import linting to catch invalid imports before UI execution
improvements.evidence: Round 3 reported "TS2305: Module 'react-native-paper' has no exported member 'View'" and the same import caused a Minified React error #130 that broke the primary flow tests (round 3 UI validator failures). The issue persisted for multiple rounds before being fixed.
improvements.change: Introduce a new static validator (typescript_import_lint.py) that runs after the planner and before the first coder turn. It should parse all .tsx files and flag any import of symbols not exported by the declared package (e.g., importing View from 'react-native-paper'). The validator’s error message must follow the actionable format from improvement 1.
improvements.expected_effect: Invalid imports are detected in round 0, preventing runtime crashes and UI flow test failures, thereby eliminating at least two full rounds of UI debugging and saving ~1 hour per run.

improvements.title: Enforce dependency‑to‑manifest consistency
improvements.evidence: Round 7 revealed "Missing dependency: Pillow not listed in backend/requirements.txt", causing an ImportError when uploading receipts. The issue was only discovered after the coder had already committed code referencing PIL.
improvements.change: Add a dependency consistency validator (dependency_check.py) to the static‑validation stage. It scans all import statements in both backend (Python) and Expo (JavaScript/TypeScript) source files, compares them against backend/requirements.txt and expo-app/package.json, and reports any missing entries with file/line details.
improvements.expected_effect: Missing packages are caught before code execution, preventing runtime import failures and reducing the need for post‑hoc dependency fixes, which should cut at least one revision round per missing package.

improvements.title: Require secure JWT secret length at project generation
improvements.evidence: Both round 1 and round 12 test logs show warnings: "JWT_SECRET_KEY is shorter than 32 bytes; this is insecure for production" and the test suite still flagged a dashboard mismatch possibly tied to token handling.
improvements.change: Modify the planner prompt to generate a JWT secret of at least 32 bytes (e.g., a 64‑character base64 string) and set it in the .env template. Add a validator (jwt_secret_length.py) that checks the length of JWT_SECRET_KEY at the start of each run and fails with a clear fix suggestion if it is too short.
improvements.expected_effect: Eliminates insecure‑key warnings, satisfies security policies on the first attempt, and removes the related test failure noise, improving both security‑scan pass rate and test stability.

improvements.title: Standardise accessibility handling for icon components
improvements.evidence: Round 1 accessibility validator reported serious issues: icons rendered as <div role="img"> lacked alternative text, and the reviewer’s suggestion was generic, resulting in the issue persisting through multiple rounds (still UI‑blocking in later rounds).
improvements.change: Extend the designer prompt with a mandatory rule: "All icon components must be hidden from the accessibility tree (aria‑hidden) unless they convey meaning. The designer must add aria‑hidden to any <Icon>, <MaterialCommunityIcons>, or PaperProvider‑generated icon and document this in DESIGN.md. Include a sample snippet." Also enhance the UI validator to flag any role="img" without aria‑hidden/aria‑label and output file/line details.
improvements.expected_effect: Accessibility validator passes from round 1 onward, removing the need for repeated UI revisions related to icons and lowering the UI‑blocking count, which speeds up convergence of UI flow tests.
